name: Lenten almond draught
long_description: This fasting-day drink is an opaque ivory emulsion, with a fine almond sediment settling slowly beneath its creamy surface.
taste: It tastes softly nutty and faintly sweet, leaving a clean almond richness without any dairy tang.
smell: Its mild scent recalls freshly crushed almonds, warm water, and a trace of honey.

name: convent walnut milk
long_description: Ground walnuts give this monastic fasting milk a pale taupe colour, a slightly grainy body, and a thin layer of oil at the rim.
taste: Deep walnut flavour brings gentle bitterness and earthy richness, rounded by a restrained touch of honey.
smell: It smells of cracked walnut shells, fresh kernels, and cool stoneware.

name: poppy-seed fast emulsion
long_description: Tiny grey seed flecks remain suspended through this light fasting emulsion, which pours smoothly despite its visibly ground texture.
taste: The drink is delicately nutty and grassy, with a mild seed bitterness at the finish.
smell: A quiet aroma of crushed poppy seed and damp meal rises from it.

name: green-grape cook's verjuice
long_description: Pressed from unripe grapes, this clear yellow-green cookery liquid has a brisk acidity and a faint natural haze near the bottom.
taste: Its first impression is sharply sour, followed by green grape, mineral freshness, and almost no sweetness.
smell: It carries the bright smell of crushed young grapes and snapped vine stems.

name: sorrel verjuice sauce
long_description: Chopped sorrel clouds this tart sauce a deep leaf-green, while strained herb fragments collect along the sides of its vessel.
taste: The sauce tastes vividly sour and leafy, with pepper and salt sharpening its clean finish.
smell: Its aroma combines bruised sorrel, green grape juice, and fresh-cut herbs.

name: clarified court hippocras
long_description: Careful straining leaves this spiced red wine brilliantly clear, with a ruby colour and no visible spice sediment.
taste: Sweet wine leads into cinnamon, ginger, and clove, then closes with warming alcohol and dry spice.
smell: It smells richly of red wine, cassia bark, ginger, and a little honey.

name: warmed peppered wine
long_description: This heated wine is dark garnet and lightly steaming, with ground pepper settling in a fine ring around the cup.
taste: Warm red wine and black pepper dominate, followed by muted sweetness and a firmly alcoholic finish.
smell: Steam carries vinous fruit, cracked pepper, and the smoky scent of the heating pot.

name: monastic bitter-herb wine
long_description: A measured steeping of bitter herbs gives this table wine a green-brown cast and leaves a few fine particles after straining.
taste: Dry wine supports wormwood-like bitterness, garden herbs, and a long medicinal warmth.
smell: Its stern fragrance suggests dried leaves, resinous stems, and pale wine.

name: honeyed pomegranate table draught
long_description: Diluted pomegranate juice colours this courtly table drink a clear crimson, with honey adding a slight viscosity to its flow.
taste: Tart red fruit arrives first, then floral honey softens the acidity and leaves a gently sweet finish.
smell: The draught smells of split pomegranate, warm honey, and fresh water.

name: infirmary barley water
long_description: Long-simmered barley has left this infirmary drink pale and faintly cloudy, with only a few grains escaping the final straining.
taste: It tastes mild, starchy, and lightly toasted, carrying little more than barley sweetness and clean water.
smell: A soft scent of boiled grain and warm earthenware hangs above it.

name: bread-thickened sickroom caudle
long_description: Fine bread crumbs thicken this warm sickroom drink to a smooth beige pour, with spice dust visible across the top.
taste: Soft wheat and warm broth give way to ginger and a modest salted richness.
smell: It smells of soaked bread, gentle spice, and recently heated stock.

name: almond-saffron caudle
long_description: Almond emulsion and saffron make this fasting caudle creamy and golden, with an occasional red thread drifting through it.
taste: Nutty almond body carries floral saffron, mild sweetness, and a warming ginger close.
smell: Its perfume blends crushed almonds, haylike saffron, and honeyed spice.

name: monastic parsley broth
long_description: This modest monastic broth is nearly clear, scattered with chopped parsley and a few softened leek threads.
taste: Fresh parsley and mild allium lift a clean salted broth with very little fat.
smell: It gives off the humble fragrance of garden herbs, leek, and steaming stock.

name: fish-day saffron broth
long_description: Saffron turns this lean fish-day broth a luminous gold, while tiny herb flecks and a pearly sheen mark its surface.
taste: A delicate briny savour is brightened by saffron, parsley, and gentle pepper.
smell: The steam smells of light fish stock, saffron threads, and chopped greens.

name: capon restoration broth
long_description: Slowly strained capon stock forms a clear amber broth with small golden beads of fat moving across the surface.
taste: It tastes deeply poultry-rich yet clean, finishing with sweet root vegetables and warming herbs.
smell: A full aroma of roasted bird, parsley roots, and pepper rises with the steam.

name: ale-onion pottage liquor
long_description: Onion-softened ale makes this pottage liquor brown and faintly opaque, with a thin foam gathering wherever it is stirred.
taste: Malted bitterness sits beneath caramelised onion, salt, and a lingering breadlike savour.
smell: It smells of dark ale, browned onions, and the warm interior of a cooking pot.

name: spiced galantine sauce
long_description: Bread and dark stock give this banquet sauce a smooth, spoon-coating body, stained brown by wine and ground spices.
taste: Sour wine, pepper, and cinnamon cut through its rich meat-stock depth with a sharp finish.
smell: Its dense aroma mixes roasted stock, wine vinegar, warm spice, and bread.

name: medieval green herb sawse
long_description: Pounded parsley and other garden herbs colour this cold sauce vivid green, with bread lending a lightly thickened texture.
taste: Fresh herbs, vinegar, and garlic make it bright, pungent, and sharply appetite-wakening.
smell: It smells intensely of crushed parsley, sour wine, garlic, and damp bread.

name: breaded garlic jance
long_description: Soaked bread and crushed garlic form a pale, creamy medieval sauce with a rougher grain than dairy cream.
taste: Strong garlic leads, softened by wheat, broth, and enough acidity to keep the sauce lively.
smell: The sauce smells of raw garlic, wet bread, and a small measure of vinegar.

name: spiced must reduction
long_description: Grape must has been simmered to a purple-brown syrup, carrying fine spice sediment and a slow, sticky pour.
taste: Concentrated grape sweetness meets cinnamon and pepper before a dark caramel finish.
smell: It has the heady scent of boiling must, dried spice, and scorched sugar.

name: quince-and-honey electuary syrup
long_description: Cooked quince and honey produce a translucent amber syrup, thick enough to trail slowly from a spoon.
taste: Floral honey surrounds tart quince, leaving a perfumed sweetness and slight fruit astringency.
smell: Its fragrance recalls poached quince, meadow honey, and a trace of warm spice.

name: late-medieval violet syrup
long_description: Steeped violet petals tint this prized syrup a delicate purple, with clarified sugar giving it a glassy consistency.
taste: The sweetness is distinctly floral, softened by cool water and a faint green petal note.
smell: It smells of fresh violets, clean sugar syrup, and spring leaves.

name: spiced monastic oxymel
long_description: Honey and vinegar mingle in this cloudy amber monastic preparation, with crushed spices settling below the surface.
taste: It tastes equally sweet and sour, followed by ginger warmth and a dry vinegar prickle.
smell: A sharp honeyed aroma carries vinegar, ginger, and bruised medicinal herbs.

name: ale-mustard trencher sauce
long_description: Ground mustard suspended in small ale makes this trencher sauce ochre and grainy, with bubbles clinging around its rim.
taste: Hot mustard bites first, then malt sweetness and light bitterness temper the heat.
smell: Its pungent smell joins crushed mustard seed, fresh ale, and sour bread.

name: oat-pottage souring liquor
long_description: A short fermentation has made this oat liquor cloudy grey and lightly effervescent, with starch settling in soft layers.
taste: Gentle lactic sourness runs through raw oat flavour, ending dry, yeasty, and faintly salty.
smell: It smells of wet oats, active yeast, and the clean tang of fermentation.
